newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse seen flat despite earnings data.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse seen flat despite earnings data.

text.p: The sideways movement seen on the Polish bourse for the last six weeks should continue next week despite expected selective stocks jumps or falls in speculation before the release of companies' monthly earnings, analysts said.
They said none of the signals expected next week was strong enough to move the market in either direction.

They said selective demand on stocks expected to show good earnings and falls on those seen reporting low profits were likely on speculation before the release of earnings figures for November, most of them due on Wednesday.
But the movements were expected to affect only smaller companies as large-caps were not vulnerable to the monthly speculation, analysts said.

"The release of the monthly figures could liven up the market and cause some speculation before the data, but it's unlikely to move the whole market," said Mateusz Andrzejewski, an analyst at Pekao SA brokerage.
The WIG index closed at 13,706.3 points, 1.3 percent higher than last Friday's close.
Analysts said the market could swing in a channel of between 13,500 and 14,000 points of the index next week.
Pekao's Andrzejewski said, however, that growing turnovers and some share market moves this week suggested the bourse could skid off the horizontal trend before Christmas.

Some analysts said Monday's inflation figures for November as well as Wednesday's food price growth for the December 1-10 period were unlikely to have an effect on the market as no interest rate change was expected.
Industrial and construction outputs in November, expected on Tuesday, might influence stocks of the industrial and construction sectors, but rather in the longer-term, they said.

Analysts said the primary market could still be drawing some capital from the bourse with two initial-public-offerings of edible-fats maker Kruszwica SA and steel products trader Centrostal SA ending on Friday next week.
They said larger investors might be staying away as well, eager to take profits before their financial year ends.
The week's top gainers were Remak, which jumped 11.9 percent, Computerland, which rose 11.3 percent and Universal gaining 10.5 percent.
The biggest losers were PPABank, which fell 6.2 percent and KPBP Bick, down 5.2 percent.
